provenance: Routing search benchmark, 2026-09-30. Andrew asked whether routing's search for earlier work would hold up in real life. Work W01 and W05 open with alerts harvested from live (testdata/learning/retained-haproxy-lifecycle.json and retained-auth-memory-recurrence.json), W06 with the harvested Slack thread in retained-draft-keep-thread.json, W02-W04 follow the world scenarios one-outage-two-channels-joins-one-episode and similar-alert-different-environment-stays-separate, W20 is the request in Andrew's screenshot; the rest are written the way the team talks. Titles are the one line Work writes when it names a request. Each message names the work it belongs to, or null for a new request. Add every real miss here. Distractors (D001-D150) are routine work a busy team has in a month, generated from templates over twenty services and six hosts so that the search has to rank, not just return everything. Follow-ups without a subject ("any update on this?") belong to the most recent running work in their channel: nothing but where and when ties them to it. W21-W25 are the first of two firings of one Grafana rule on one host from the Tenant alert history (2026-09-01 to 09-04, the Grafana host renamed), and the five alert messages are the second firing of each: three are Traefik rules worded alike, told apart only by the rule page their title links to (ID6 and ID7, 2026-09-30).
